messages.displayText:
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Tourist Tips<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> like this one contain useful information
that will help you as you explore Lumiose City.

You’ll keep uncovering more tips as your adventure
progresses. If you press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0001>L on the main menu and
select the Tourist Tips option, you can refer back to all
the tips you’ve unlocked so far.

The <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>autosave function <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>will automatically save your
progress for you as you play. You can also manually
save your game by pressing <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0001>R on the main menu.

If you close your game, you’ll resume your adventure
from wherever your progress was last saved.

When a Pokémon is ready to evolve, you’ll see an
arrow icon displayed on its image in your party.

Select a Pokémon that has this icon and choose the
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Evolve <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>option to trigger its Evolution!

The map app shows you the names of areas and
information about various facilities around Lumiose.
It also has a handy <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>guidance feature <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>that can help you
find your next destination.

Check the map at any time when you’re out exploring
the city by pressing <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Plus.

From your map, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_1 to open your mission list,
then <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0001>L and <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0001>R to switch between the two tabs and
check the details of the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>missions<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> you currently have.

If you have multiple missions ongoing, you can also
change which one you want guidance enabled for.

Major locations will be registered on your map as soon
as you visit them. Once they’re registered, you’ll be
able to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>travel back to them in an instant<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

You can either select the icon for a specific travel spot
directly on your map or press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_2 to open the full list of
travel spots to choose from.

The goals you try to achieve as part of Team MZ are
referred to as <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>main missions<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

When you’re feeling lost or unsure about what to do
next, check the guidance provided in your mission list
to help you find your way!

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Side missions<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> are small requests that you take on to
serve the people of Lumiose City.

You can earn rewards for helping your fellow citizens,
so whenever you see a blue and white icon on your
map or above a person, be sure to check it out!

You will receive requests from Mable to help her with
her research.

As you complete her tasks, your <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>research level <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>will go
up and you’ll also receive <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>valuable rewards<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>, such as
TMs, so keep an eye out for new tasks as they are
continually added!

At times, you may have several main missions become
available at once.

You are free to take them on in whichever order you
prefer. You can choose a mission you’d like to tackle
from your mission list, then <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>turn on guidance<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> for it if
you’d like help reaching your destination.

Pokémon can be sent to your Boxes for safekeeping.
You can <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>access the Pokémon in your Boxes<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> anytime—
as long as you aren’t in the middle of a battle!

When you heal your party Pokémon at a Pokémon
Center, the Pokémon in your Boxes will have their
health restored as well.

The Judge feature gives you a concrete evaluation of
your individual Pokémon’s stats so you can <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>gauge their<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>latent potential<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

From the Stats section of your Pokémon’s summary,
press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_R_Push to toggle between numbers and what the
Judge feature says about each stat.

Having this app on your smartphone allows you to
build up a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>record of Pokémon <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>that you encounter
in Lumiose City.

Data will be registered whenever you obtain a
Pokémon—such as by catching it, via Evolution,
or by receiving it from another Trainer.

This app is for Trainers taking part in the Z-A Royale.
It lets you check key stats about your current standing,
including your rank and how many points you have.

Whenever an opponent has been decided for your
next <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>promotion match<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>, this app will also show you
who you will be facing.

Earn yourself a Challenger’s Ticket and show it to the
receptionist at Quasartico Inc. for a chance to battle in
a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>reward match<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>. If you win the match, amazing prizes
will be yours to keep!

After each reward match, your Ticket Points will be
reset to zero.

You can change your <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>outfit <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>and <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>looks<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> by pressing <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0005>Minus
while on the main menu.

If you buy new clothing and accessories at boutiques,
you’ll be able to switch up your style in more and more
ways. Have fun finding a look that’s all your own!

Clothing items labeled as a “set” have multiple parts to
them, which you can <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>customize as an ensemble<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

For example, if you have the same jacket and shirt set
in different designs, you can mix ’n’ match the jackets
and shirts to create fresh looks. Pick out your favorite
colors and patterns, and show off your styling skills!

When you select a Pokémon from the main menu,
you can also <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>change what moves<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> you want it to have
access to.

When one of your Pokémon learns a new move, try
setting it as one of your Pokémon’s current moves
so you can see what it does.

TMs allow you to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>teach moves to your Pokémon<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.
They can be used however many times you like!

Each Pokémon species is able to learn a different
selection of moves.

You can use the camera in your Rotom Phone to
take photos of the scenery around Lumiose City
or to capture moments you’d like to remember.

Photos you take will be saved in your system’s <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Album<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

Hold down <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZL to focus on the opposing Pokémon
you want to target, then use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0006>Decide or other buttons to
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>order your Pokémon to use moves<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

Once all the opposing Trainer’s Pokémon have had
their HP reduced to zero, you win!

To get your Pokémon ready to Mega Evolve, you must
give it a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Mega Stone<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> to hold.

Select one of your Pokémon from the main menu, then
choose “Give an item to hold” or “Change held item” to
give your Pokémon a Mega Stone.

Your Pokémon will need the specific Mega Stone that
corresponds to its species.

For example, Absol will not be able to Mega Evolve
unless you give it an <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Absolite stone<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> to hold.

When your Mega Ring is full of Mega Power, give
your Pokémon the signal to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Mega Evolve <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>with <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_R_Push!

Your accumulated Mega Power will start draining as
soon as you trigger Mega Evolution. Once the power
is gone, your Pokémon will revert to its usual form. But
it can Mega Evolve again if you store up more power!

Use moves as Plus Moves to increase their strength by
draining some power from your Mega Ring. Only moves
with a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Plus Move mark<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> can be used as Plus Moves!

During battle, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Plus before choosing a move to use
it as a Plus Move. While a Pokémon is Mega Evolved,
its moves are automatically used as Plus Moves.

Every Pokémon has at least one <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>type<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>. There are
eighteen types in total.

Chikorita is a Grass type. Tepig is a Fire type.
Totodile is a Water type.

When a Pokémon is hit by an attack, the damage
calculation takes into account <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>that Pokémon’s type<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
and <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>the move’s type<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

“Supereffective” attacks deal more damage, while
“not very effective” attacks deal less.

The column on the left shows the type of the attacking
move, and the row at the top shows the type of the
defending Pokémon. The results for each matchup are
indicated using the following four symbols.

　◎: Super effective
　〇: No weakness or resistance
　△: Not very effective
　 ×: No effect

When Pokémon undergo <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Rogue Mega Evolution<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>, they
gain formidable strength and become hard to damage.

You may not be able to defeat one without a Mega-
Evolved Pokémon of your own.

When you attack a Rogue Mega-Evolved Pokémon,
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>orbs of Mega Power<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> will burst out of it. Collecting
them will fill your Mega Ring with this power.

Once your Mega Ring is fully charged, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_R_Push to
Mega Evolve your Pokémon and fight back!

Zygarde has three different forms: 10% Forme,
50% Forme, and Complete Forme.

You can use a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Zygarde Cube<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> to freely switch Zygarde
between its 10% Forme and 50% Forme.

If its <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>HP drops to<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>half or less<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> during battle, Zygarde
will change into its Complete Forme.

In this form, all Zygarde Cores and Zygarde Cells have
gathered, increasing Zygarde’s stats significantly.

Zygarde can Mega Evolve only when in its
Complete Forme.

When Zygarde becomes Mega Zygarde, its
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Core Enforcer<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> move transforms into <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Nihil Light<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

If you want to catch a wild Pokémon, you’ll need to
throw a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Poké Ball<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>!

First, use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZL to focus on your target Pokémon.

Then you can press and hold <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZR to aim a Poké Ball.

When you’re ready to throw, <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>let go<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> of <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZR to let your
Poké Ball fly! If the ball hits a wild Pokémon, it may
result in a successful catch.

If you have a Poké Ball ready but want to cancel your
throw, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0006>Cancel.

The more you lower your target’s HP, the better your
chances of a successful catch.

In fact, if you defeat the target in battle, you’ll have a
brief <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>catch window<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>—a moment where the Pokémon
becomes far easier to catch. Act fast!

If you keep pelting the same Pokémon with Poké Balls,
you may anger it.

While it’s angry, <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>it can’t be caught<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>—Poké Balls will
bounce right off it. You’ll have to wait until it calms
down before trying again.

If a <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>wild Pokémon<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> attacks you, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000B>Button_Left or <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Button_Right to
choose a Pokémon from your party, then press <U+0010><U+0002>봊	Button_Up to
send it out and fight back.

To call your Pokémon back to its Poké Ball, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000B>Button_Down.

But be careful—if you don’t have a Pokémon out, wild
Pokémon will <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>attack you directly<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>. If you take too many
hits, you’ll black out!

When you use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZL to focus on a wild Pokémon, you can
see details like its name, its level, and how easy it will
be to catch.

The more <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Λ <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>symbols you see next to a Pokémon, the
better your chances of catching it.

Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0006>Cancel to dash.

There’s no need to hold the button down—you will
continue to dash as long as you keep moving.

Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_2 to dive and roll.

Doing so will let you dodge the attacks of aggressive
Pokémon and avoid taking damage.

Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_L_Push to crouch.

You can hide by crouching behind objects, making you
harder to spot.

Crouching in patches of <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>tall grass<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> will hide your
presence even better.

When falling from someplace high, you can press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0006>Decide
to Roto-Glide.

Roto-Gliding uses a short burst of the Rotom Phone’s
safe landing mode to give you a momentary lift, letting
you <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>move while in midair<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

Wild zones are sectioned-off areas in Lumiose City
where wild Pokémon can live in conditions similar to
their natural habitats. If you go into one, you may be
attacked by aggressive Pokémon, but you’ll have plenty
of chances to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>catch Pokémon <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>as well!

Find wild zones by pressing <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Plus to open your map.

Inside battle zones, you’ll find lots of Trainers taking
part in the Z-A Royale.

These Trainers will challenge you to battle on sight.
Defeat them to earn <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Ticket Points<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>!

As you approach Trainers in battle zones, they’ll start
to become aware of you. Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_L_Push to crouch, and hide
behind objects or buildings to avoid being spotted.

If the Trainers notice you and challenge you to battle,
you may be caught off guard and become <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>unable to<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>move<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> for a short while.

If you can sneak up on a Trainer and hit their Pokémon
with a move before they notice you, you’ll gain an
advantage from getting that <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>first strike<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

These first strikes also deal more damage than usual.

Defeating Trainers in a battle zone will earn you
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>prize medals<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

But be careful—battle zone rules cut both ways!
If you lose a battle, you’ll have to give up half your
prize medals.

You can also pick up prize medals that you find lying
around battle zones.

When daybreak comes, you’ll receive <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>prize money<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
based on how many medals you collected.

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Bonus cards<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> can be found in various places around
battle zones.

These special cards let you earn additional points or
medals if you fulfill the conditions listed on them.
You can carry up to three cards at a time.

Need a break? You can <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>pass some time<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> on the benches
located throughout the city.

Just grab a seat, and time will pass in the blink of an
eye—whether from night to day or day to night.

Join up to three other Trainers in a frenetic free-for-all
battle! The Trainer who can defeat the most of their
opponents’ Pokémon within the time limit wins!

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>You can switch your Pokémon up to three times<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.
Think hard about which one you send out and when.

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>The moment one of your Pokémon faints<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>, you’ll be sent
back to your starting point.

When this happens, your Pokémon will be fully healed
and the limit for how many times you can switch your
Pokémon will be reset to three.

When you pick up a glowing item, its effects will
instantly be applied to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>your whole party of Pokémon<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

These items have a range of useful effects depending
on their color. For example, they may recover your
Pokémon’s HP or grant temporary stat boosts.

In Ranked Battles, you can use the internet to take on
Trainers from around the world.

Take part in plenty of battles to earn points and aim to
reach the highest rank you can within set periods.

Ranked Battles take place during set periods called
seasons. At the start of each new season, <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>your rank<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>and accumulated points will be reset<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

You can earn different rewards based on what rank you
reach by the end of a season.

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Different species of Pokémon<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> will be eligible to take
part in Ranked Battles each season.

Once the rules for a new season are available, you can
view them by selecting Link Play from the main menu,
then checking the news.

You can assign yourself titles that will be displayed to
other players along with your name.

New titles will become available as you meet the
required conditions. When you earn one that’s right
for you, choose it to show your opponents who they’re
dealing with!

Complete these missions to demystify the strange
dimension that seems to be leaking into Lumiose City!

You can take on these missions alongside your main
missions and side missions, so change which mission
has <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>guidance<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> enabled as needed and aim to tackle as
many as you can!

If you give Ansha three Berries, she can make a donut
for you.

The kind of donut you’ll get will depend on the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>effects<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
and <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>flavors<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> of the Berries used as ingredients.

A donut’s <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Level Boost<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> will increase the levels of all the
Pokémon in your party by the number shown.

This boost can provide an important leg up in battle
against high-level opponents in Hyperspace Lumiose.

The <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Donut Energy<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> Hoopa receives from a donut will
determine how long you can remain in hyperspace.

You’ll want to take this into account if you hope to take
your time exploring Hyperspace Lumiose.

If you’re lucky, a donut can also provide special effects
called <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Flavor Powers<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

These effects can provide a range of benefits, from
aiding your Pokémon in battle to helping you catch the
Pokémon you seek. Consider your current goals when
choosing which donut to use!

Pay attention to the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>rank<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> of each pocket of hyperspace
as indicated by the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>number of stars<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> (up to <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>5★<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> max)
when heading into Hyperspace Lumiose.

If you choose a lower-ranked donut, your Level Boost
and Donut Energy might not be high enough, and your
attempts to catch Pokémon will be more likely to fail.

Certain curious Berries are found only in hyperspace,
such as the Hyper Pecha Berry or Hyper Oran Berry.

These Hyperspace Berries have more powerful effects
and stronger flavors than regular Berries, so they can
produce <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>higher-ranked donuts<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Hyperspace distortions<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> have appeared all over the city,
serving as entry points into Hyperspace Lumiose. They
can be located using the handy icons on your map.

Old distortions close and new distortions appear at
sunrise and sunset each day.

With your map app open, you can press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0005>Minus to hide
other icons and <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>show distortions only<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

Removing information unrelated to hyperspace
distortions should simplify things and let you focus on
your hyperspace survey work!

When you give Hoopa a donut to eat, it will open up a
portal that allows you to enter hyperspace.

Check the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>description of each hyperspace distortion<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
and choose the <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>most suitable donut<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> for that distortion,
then off you go to survey Hyperspace Lumiose!

As time passes within a pocket of hyperspace, Hoopa’s
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Donut Energy<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> will gradually be consumed. Once it runs
out, you’ll have to halt your survey work and return to
regular Lumiose.

You’ll also have to leave hyperspace if you black out or
are defeated in battle.

When you enter a pocket of hyperspace, you’ll be
given <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>three survey tasks<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> to accomplish. Check what
you should focus on doing before you set out.

By completing these tasks and earning points, you’ll
help propel the work of Corbeau and his team.

While battling Rogue Mega-Evolved Pokémon in
Hyperspace Lumiose, you’ll want to keep an eye on
how much <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Donut Energy<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> Hoopa has left.

Picking up <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>black energy orbs <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>during the battle will
pause the consumption of Hoopa’s Donut Energy,
giving you more time to seize victory.

This Pokédex registers <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Pokémon found in hyperspace<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.
There are many curious species living there that aren’t
normally found in Lumiose City!

Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_1 in the Pokédex menu to switch between your
Lumiose Pokédex and Hyperspace Pokédex.

If you earn enough points from completing survey
tasks, you’ll be able carry out a special scan for a
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>hyperspace distortion with a five-star rank (5★)<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

A distortion found via special scan will stay open until
you enter it. But if you perform another special scan,
the one you had previously located will disappear.

Certain hyperspace distortions newly appearing on
your map can grant you a chance to battle Rogue
Mega-Evolved Pokémon you’ve previously defeated.

These Rogue Pokémon boast extraordinary hyperspace
levels, but defeating them will reward you with <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>lots of<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>
<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>survey points<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000> and <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>rare, valuable Hyperspace Berries<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

If you give Groudon a Red Orb to hold, you can have it
undergo Primal Reversion in battle to revert it to its
primal state: <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Primal Groudon<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

If you give Kyogre a Blue Orb to hold, you can have it
undergo Primal Reversion in battle to revert it to its
primal state: <U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0006>Primal Kyogre<U+0010><U+0002>＀<U+0000>.

If you give Groudon a Red Orb to hold, you can have it
undergo Primal Reversion in battle to revert it to its
